issues.title: Parallel combine and parallel source for large perfect hash aggregate (re-land E0001)
issues.hypothesis: E0001 cut q13's inner aggregate operator CPU from 3.14s to 0.53s, but wall time improved only 3.6%. I re-checked this round with SET perfect_ht_threshold=22: the PERFECT_HASH_GROUP_BY takes 0.45s, HASH_JOIN 1.59s and the scan about 2.4s, so about 4.4s of CPU in total, which is about 0.55s if spread over 8 threads. Wall time is still about 0.72-0.86s, the same as the radix-HA baseline (whose CPU of about 6.8s divided by 8 matches its wall time). So about 0.25s of the plan is serial. The code shows where. (1) PhysicalPerfectHashAggregate::Combine (physical_perfecthash_aggregate.cpp:164) takes one global mutex and calls PerfectAggregateHashTable::Combine (perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp:163), which walks all 2^bits slots of each local table. With 8 threads and 2M slots that is 16M slot visits, one table at a time. (2) PerfectHashAggregateState (source, line 178) has one shared ht_scan_position and no parallel source support. So the scan of 2M slots, FinalizeStates, and everything downstream (decompress projection, outer HASH_GROUP_BY over 1.5M rows) run on one thread. The radix HA baseline has a parallel source, so switching to the perfect HA made the downstream pipeline serial. That cancelled E0001's CPU win.
issues.plan: (a) Re-land E0001's CanUsePerfectHashAggregate extension in src/execution/physical_plan/plan_aggregate.cpp (around line 127) with the same three guards: total bits at most max(threshold, 22); density, meaning estimated_cardinality >= 2^bits/4; and memory, meaning threads * 2^bits * (aligned state size + 1) <= max_memory/8. Keep the existing threshold path unchanged. (b) Add PerfectAggregateHashTable::CombineRange(other, begin, end, ArenaAllocator &alloc). It is Combine restricted to slots [begin,end), using a RowOperationsState built on the caller-provided arena. Moving other's aggregate_allocator into stored_allocators becomes a separate step done under the global lock. (c) In PerfectHashAggregateGlobalState, add a fixed array of stripe mutexes (for example 64 stripes, each a multiple of STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE slots) and an atomic start counter. Use the striped path only when total_groups >= 2^16. Small tables keep the existing single-lock path, so behaviour is unchanged for default-threshold queries. In Combine, each thread starts at stripe (atomic++ % S), visits every stripe in rotation, locks it and runs CombineRange into the global table with its own local ArenaAllocator. Afterwards, under the global lock, it pushes that arena and the local table's arena into stored_allocators. (d) Make the source parallel. Override MaxThreads in the global source state (ceil(total_groups / block) for large tables, 1 for small). Hand out blocks of slots (for example 2048*8) through an atomic counter. Add a per-thread LocalSourceState holding the current block range and its own ArenaAllocator for FinalizeStates. Add a PerfectAggregateHashTable::Scan overload that takes an end position. Check whether PhysicalPerfectHashAggregate already declares ParallelSource/GetLocalSourceState and set them as needed. Output order is not guaranteed for hash aggregates, so a parallel source is semantically fine.
issues.expected_gain: q13: 10-20%. It removes about 0.15-0.25s of serial combine and source work while keeping E0001's 2.6s CPU saving.
issues.generality: Any GROUP BY on dense integer keys with a large range (surrogate ids, dates, keys compressed to uinteger), for example per-customer and per-order counts or sums. Small perfect HAs (the default threshold of 12 bits or fewer) keep the exact old code path. Possible slowdowns: sparse key ranges that pass the density estimate wrongly. These are bounded by the density and memory guards.
issues.risk: Medium. The arena allocator must never be shared between threads, so each combine and scan thread gets its own arena that is stored afterwards. Aggregates with destructors (Destroy loop) must still see each state exactly once. Stripe bounds must cover every slot. Results must be checked on aggregates beyond count (sum, min/max on strings, list) through hidden validation.
